accessibility.text: Let’s take stock. We’ve now considered three candidate rules of belief.
One way to underline the force of the evidentialist argument is to use the example of one of the world’s fastest growing religions: Pastafarianism.
No Proof → No Belief
If you can’t give a good argument for P, don’t believe P.
We’ve seen that both of our “no belief” principles are open to substantial challenge. But surely, one might think, there must be some principle which explains why certain beliefs are bad beliefs.
Proof → Belief
If you can prove P, believe P.
Doubt → No Belief
If you cannot distinguish between a situation in which P and a situation in which not-P, do not believe P.
